A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PK(c) from bananas has a pH optimum of approximately 7, and is inhibited by MgATP, activated by L-aspartate, and inhibited by L-glutamine.
the banana PK(c) is a typical cytosolic PK with a pH optimum of pH 7.0, and that it is a homotetramer of subunits of about 57 kDa, with a molecular mass of about 240 kDa.
cytosolic pyrophosphate-dependent PEP carboxykinase is the primary PEP-consuming enzyme in ripening banana fruit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PK(c) is a major target for the regulation of the PEP node in ripening banana fruit.
cytosolic PK is the most efficient and specific enzyme in the banana fruit for converting PEP to pyruvate, and it is therefore a key regulatory enzyme for the PEP branch point.

the cytosolic pH of ripening banana fruits is a key determinant of the relative activities of cytosolic PK and PEP carboxykinase, and thus of the partitioning of carbon between glycolysis and the TCA cycle.
